# Test fixtures

Binary inputs the unit tests read with `include_bytes!`, so they must stay checked in and
must not be regenerated by a build script or a test.

## `lz4/` — LZ4 frame decoder (`src/archive_lz4.rs`)

Each `.lz4` file is paired with the plain file it expands to; the test decodes the frame and
compares, so the pair is the expectation. Produced with the `lz4` CLI 1.9.4 on Linux x86-64;
the commands are deterministic, and running them again on that version reproduces every
file byte for byte. A different `lz4` version may pick different match offsets inside the
same frame — regenerate both the `.lz4` and its `.txt` and the test still passes.

Every file here is compared byte for byte, so `.gitattributes` marks `tests/fixtures/**`
as `-text`: without that, `* text=auto` would give a Windows checkout CRLF in the `.txt`
files while the frames keep LF, and the comparison would fail for a reason that has nothing
to do with the decoder.

```sh
: > empty.txt
printf 'a' > one-byte.txt
python3 -c '
words = ["alpha", "needle", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "lorem", "ipsum", "dolor", "sit",
         "amet", "consectetur", "adipiscing", "elit", "sed", "tempor"]
body, n, i = [], 0, 0
while n < 102400:
    line = "line %d: %s %s %d the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog\n" % (
        i, words[i % len(words)], words[(i * 7) % len(words)], (i * 37) % 1000)
    body.append(line)
    n += len(line)
    i += 1
open("mixed-100k.txt", "w").write("".join(body)[:102400])
'
python3 -c '
import hashlib
seed, buf, i = b"dusage lz4 fixture", bytearray(), 0
while len(buf) < 102400:
    buf += hashlib.sha256(seed + str(i).encode()).digest()
    i += 1
open("random-100k.txt", "wb").write(bytes(buf[:102400]))
'

lz4 -q -z -f empty.txt empty.lz4
lz4 -q -z -f one-byte.txt one-byte.lz4
lz4 -q -z -f mixed-100k.txt mixed-100k.lz4
lz4 -q -z -f -B4 mixed-100k.txt multiblock.lz4
lz4 -q -z -f -BD -B4 mixed-100k.txt linked.lz4
lz4 -q -z -f -B4 random-100k.txt uncompressed.lz4
lz4 -q -z -f --content-size -BX mixed-100k.txt checksum-size.lz4
cat mixed-100k.lz4 one-byte.lz4 > concatenated.lz4
```

| file | expands to | what it exercises |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `empty.lz4` | `empty.txt` | a frame with no blocks: descriptor, end mark, content checksum only |
| `one-byte.lz4` | `one-byte.txt` | the smallest stored block, 64 KiB block size code |
| `mixed-100k.lz4` | `mixed-100k.txt` | one compressed block of 100 KiB text, 256 KiB block size code |
| `multiblock.lz4` | `mixed-100k.txt` | two compressed blocks with `-B4` (64 KiB), independent |
| `linked.lz4` | `mixed-100k.txt` | `-BD`: linked blocks, where a match reaches into the block before it |
| `uncompressed.lz4` | `random-100k.txt` | stored (uncompressed) blocks: incompressible input, block size bit 31 set |
| `checksum-size.lz4` | `mixed-100k.txt` | a content size in the descriptor, plus block and content checksums |
| `concatenated.lz4` | `mixed-100k.txt` then `one-byte.txt` | two frames back to back, one of them a stored block |

`-BD` in the LZ4 CLI means *block dependency*, not "uncompressed": a frame with stored
blocks is what the CLI writes when the data does not compress, which is why
`uncompressed.lz4` comes from the SHA-256 stream.
